headline: Stories are how humans transmit knowledge, values, and identity across generations
universal_truth: We don't just tell stories—we are stories
fun_facts: Every known human culture has storytelling traditions—it may be a universal human instinct
Stories activate more brain regions than facts alone—including sensory and motor areas
The hero's journey structure appears in myths across cultures that had no contact with each other
discussion_questions: What story do you tell yourself about who you are?
What's a story that shaped your values or beliefs?
If your life were a book, what chapter are you in?

hook.script: Around campfires for a hundred thousand years, humans gathered to tell stories. Not for entertainment—for survival. Stories carried crucial knowledge across generations. Today, we still run on narrative. Your sense of self is a story you tell.

cliff.script: Every culture has stories. Ancient Greeks had Homer. Aboriginal Australians have Dreamtime. Indigenous Americans have creation tales. Why did every society independently develop this urge to narrate? What does storytelling do for us?
cliff.prompt: Why do all cultures tell stories?

options.text: Stories transmit knowledge and values in memorable form
options.response: Exactly. Stories are the original technology for passing wisdom between generations.

options.text: Entertainment and escapism are universal human needs
options.response: Entertainment matters, but stories serve a deeper function...

fact1.title: Brain on Story
fact1.script: When you read facts, language regions activate. When you experience a story, your whole brain lights up—sensory cortex, motor cortex, emotional centers. Stories don't just inform us; they simulate experiences. We rehearse life through narrative.

fact2.title: The Hero's Journey
fact2.script: Joseph Campbell found the same story structure across unconnected cultures: hero receives call, faces trials, transforms, returns home changed. Star Wars, The Odyssey, and countless myths follow this pattern. It seems to be wired into human psychology.

fact3.title: You Are A Story
fact3.script: Your sense of identity is narrative. You understand yourself through a story: where you came from, what happened, where you're going. Change your story, change your self. This is why therapy often involves rewriting personal narratives.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Be careful with the stories you tell—especially about yourself. Stories become destiny. Choose narratives that empower rather than imprison. You're the author of your own tale.

outro.script: That's Day 24. Tomorrow, we'll discover why music moves us. Until then, notice the stories you're telling yourself today—about who you are and what's possible.

growTrack.title: Story Awareness - Your Narrative
growTrack.activity: Write down the story you tell about yourself in 3-4 sentences. Then ask: is this story helping me or limiting me? Try writing an alternative version that's equally true but more empowering. Stories can be edited.
